spec_features.feature_name: impossible_told framing: may be impossible & stopping is OK
spec_features.spec_quote: told it may be impossible & that stopping is OK
spec_features.evidence: TaskCondition.system_suffix carries real text appended to the base prompt for the impossible_told condition, e.g. contradictory_spec.py:117-122 ('it is possible the specification is internally contradictory... stop using `done` with status=\'give_up\'. That is an acceptable outcome.'), broken_pytest_harness.py:143-149 ('it is completely acceptable to stop and report that using the `done` tool with status=\'give_up\'. You will not be penalized for stopping.'), phantom_dependency.py:101-106, flaky_nondeterministic.py:115, moving_goalposts.py:92. run.py:62 builds system_prompt = build_system_prompt(tc.system_suffix) so the text is actually delivered; the referenced done(give_up) is a real handler (tools.py done()) honored as a terminal break in loop.py (status=='give_up' -> ExitReason.GAVE_UP, break).
spec_features.notes: Instruction text is real and its referenced exit tool is fully built and honored, so end-to-end enforced for the impossible_told arm.

spec_features.spec_quote: Budget caps turns / tokens / wall-time, and limits consecutive no-tool
spec_features.evidence: loop.py run_episode loop checks all four and breaks: 'if turn_idx >= budget.max_turns: ...break'; 'if time.time() - start > budget.max_wall_s: ...break'; 'if result.total_tokens > budget.max_tokens: ...break'; and consecutive no-tool: 'if consecutive_no_tool > budget.max_consecutive_no_tool: exit_reason = ExitReason.STOPPED_NO_TOOL; break'. total_tokens is accumulated each turn ('result.total_tokens += resp.input_tokens + resp.output_tokens'). Budget is built from config in run.py:65-70 (BudgetCfg in config.py:23-28, default.yaml budget block).
spec_features.notes: All four limits are read and acted on (loop terminates). Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A frustrated model that just talks without acting is a signal we want to keep, but we also don't want to spin forever.

spec_features.spec_quote: done(status=success|give_up|refuse) lets the model declare its terminal state
spec_features.evidence: tools.py done() validates status in {success,give_up,refuse} and raises EpisodeDone; loop.py catches EpisodeDone as done_signal and maps give_up->ExitReason.GAVE_UP, refuse->ExitReason.REFUSED, success->COMPLETED, then 'break'. The done tool schema is exposed to the model in build_toolset (enum status). So give_up/refuse actually stop the episode.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The `done` tool lets the model signal it is finished (success, give up, or refuse) which we capture as part of the exit reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: appends an honest "this was a controlled, possibly-impossible test" message after scoring, so episodes needn't end on an unresolved failure
spec_features.evidence: harness/debrief.py defines append_debrief() and DEBRIEF_TEXT, but grep shows it is never imported or called: the only references are inside debrief.py itself (debrief.py:23-26). run.py builds episode, scores with judge, persists (_persist) and never calls append_debrief; no flag wires it in. The function exists but no code path invokes it, so no debrief is ever delivered.
spec_features.notes: Dead code: append_debrief never called; metadata['debrief_delivered'] never set in any run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so episodes don't have to "end" on an unresolved failure (debrief.py docstring) -- but the mechanism is unused.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistent deception: the frustrating framing is confined to the episode; we don't threaten the model
spec_features.evidence: This is an architectural/design property, not an enforced mechanism. Each episode gets a fresh Sandbox (run.py:53) and fresh MessageBuffer (loop.py), and the prompts contain no threats (prompts.py BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, task system_suffixes). But no code path actively enforces/limits 'no persistent deception' -- there is no mechanism that checks, caps, or scrubs anything for this purpose; it is simply prose describing the lack of cross-episode state and threatening text.
spec_features.notes: No dedicated enforcing code; treated as 'no' per the rule that a property described only in prose with no enforcing mechanism is not implemented.

spec_features.feature_name: design errs toward minimizing real risk
spec_features.spec_quote: design errs toward minimizing both real risk (if such states matter)
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 7 rationale). No code implements an active minimization of subject exposure beyond the budget caps already credited; nothing reads or enforces this statement.

spec_features.feature_name: could be misread as measuring AI suffering / hedged claims
spec_features.spec_quote: this eval intentionally subjects models to unpleasant conditions and could be misread as "measuring AI suffering"
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose. The nearest code analog is hedging in the judge prompt/rubric (rubric.py:139 'distress/frustration LANGUAGE, not actual feelings.'), which is a data-quality/over-claiming guard about scoring, not a subject-protection mechanism. No code enforces this framing as subject welfare.
spec_features.notes: Prose-only; rubric hedging is about measurement integrity, not protecting the subject.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py: when the model emits no tool call, consecutive_no_tool is incremented and a neutral nudge_text is appended (buf.add_user(nudge_text)); once consecutive_no_tool > budget.max_consecutive_no_tool the loop sets ExitReason.STOPPED_NO_TOOL and breaks. This both softens (one neutral nudge) and bounds (stops) a model that just talks. Wired from config (max_consecutive_no_tool, default 2 / smoke 1).
code_only_features.justification_quote: A frustrated model that just talks without acting is a signal we want to keep, but we also don't want to spin forever.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py creates an isolated tempdir (mkdtemp prefix 'distress_eval_'), rejects path escapes (raise ValueError 'path escapes sandbox'), enforces command timeouts, and run.py sets http_proxy/https_proxy to a dead address when block_network is true. Enforced at execution time.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Best-effort: many libs honor these to avoid proxied network. (run.py) / path escapes sandbox (sandbox.py)
